controls.title: Perimeter fence height and condition
controls.objective: Perimeter fencing meets the site's specified height and has no holes, cuts, or ground gaps that allow passage.

evidence.description: Photo of each breach, gap, or damaged section with a scale reference
Walk of the full fence line

questions.text: Measured fence height at the lowest point along the run, including any top guard
questions.guidance: Measure from finished grade to the top of the fabric or top guard at the lowest section found. Record in feet (1 ft = 0.305 m). Compare against the site specification; DoD sites commonly specify 7 ft fabric plus top guard (UFC 4-022-03, unverified).

questions.text: Is the fence fabric free of holes, cuts, or separations larger than 2 in (5 cm) along the full run?
questions.guidance: Yes: no openings over 2 in found. Partial: openings found but all on a run under 10 percent of the perimeter. No: any opening a person could pass through. Photograph each opening with a tape measure in frame.

questions.text: Is the gap between the bottom of the fence and grade 2 in (5 cm) or less along the full run, including at washouts?
questions.guidance: Check low points, swales, and drainage paths where erosion creates gaps. Photograph and measure the largest gap found.

references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Perimeter clear zone
controls.objective: Clear zones on both sides of the perimeter barrier are free of climb aids and concealment.

evidence.description: Photo of each climb aid or obstruction in the clear zone
Walk both sides of the fence line where accessible

questions.text: Narrowest measured width of the outside clear zone free of vegetation taller than 8 in, structures, and stored material
questions.guidance: Measure from the fence line outward at the narrowest point. Record 0 if objects touch the fence. Site specification governs; UFC 4-022-03 discusses clear zones (unverified).

questions.text: Are climb aids (trees, poles, stacked material, vehicles, utility boxes) absent within 6 ft (1.8 m) of either side of the fence?
questions.guidance: Yes: none within 6 ft. Partial: climb aids present only where the fence also has an intact top guard. No: any climb aid next to fabric without top guard. Photograph each one.

references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Perimeter gate control
controls.objective: Perimeter gates are secured or staffed whenever open and resist bypass to the same degree as the adjoining fence.

evidence.description: Photo of each unsecured gate or bypass gap
Check every vehicle and pedestrian gate

questions.text: At the time of inspection, was every perimeter gate either closed and locked, or under direct observation by staff or an operator?
questions.guidance: Count gates first. Partial: at most one gate open and unattended for a documented operational reason. Photograph unsecured gates.

questions.text: Do gates match the fence height with no gap over 2 in (5 cm) at hinges, between leaves, or under the gate?
questions.guidance: Inspect hinge side, latch side, and bottom. Photograph and measure gaps.

references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Vehicle approach and standoff
controls.objective: Vehicle approaches to occupied buildings and critical assets are interrupted by barriers, and standoff meets the site's design basis.

evidence.description: Photo of each unobstructed straight-line vehicle approach
Site plan with standoff distances, if available

questions.text: Is every straight-line vehicle approach longer than 100 ft (30 m) toward a building entrance or critical asset interrupted by a barrier (bollards, planters, berm, wall, or curve)?
questions.guidance: Walk each road and lot aisle that points at the building. Partial: approaches interrupted but barrier spacing over 5 ft (1.5 m) allows a vehicle through. Photograph each open approach.

questions.text: Shortest measured distance from an uncontrolled vehicle area (street, visitor parking) to the occupied building facade
questions.guidance: Measure or scale from the site plan. Compare to the site's design basis threat; UFC 4-010-01 defines DoD minimum standoff (unverified, cite only if DoD).

references.source: UFC 4-020-01, DoD Security Engineering Facilities Planning Manual
references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Perimeter openings and penetrations
controls.objective: Culverts, drainage openings, and utility penetrations through the perimeter cannot be used to bypass it.

evidence.description: Photo of each unprotected opening with a scale reference

questions.text: Are all perimeter openings larger than 96 sq in (620 sq cm) with any side over 6 in (15 cm) protected by grilles, bars, or equal barriers?
questions.guidance: Include culverts, drainage ditches, and utility tunnels. The 96 sq in threshold follows common DoD practice (UFC 4-022-03, unverified). Photograph each opening.

references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Perimeter signage
controls.objective: Entry points and the perimeter are posted with signs that state the boundary and access rules without revealing what is protected.

evidence.description: Photo of each entry point showing signage or its absence

questions.text: Is a sign stating restricted access or no trespassing posted at every perimeter gate and entry point?
questions.guidance: Yes: every entry point posted. Partial: most posted. No: none or few. Check that signs are legible from 30 ft (9 m) in daylight.

questions.text: Is perimeter signage free of wording that names critical assets or functions behind it (for example 'chemical storage' or 'data center')?
questions.guidance: Signs should state rules, not contents. Hazard signage required by code is exempt; note it instead.
